title: The Seventy-Fifth Sun
story:
Seventy-five mornings had passed since James first stepped away from the cool green shade of the Great Canopy. Seventy-five mornings of watching sunrises over unfamiliar horizons. Seventy-five mornings of adjusting the weathered leather strap across his shoulder and wondering what lay past the next bend. Under the sprawling pepper tree, the early mountain air was crisp and dry. Beside him, Nico was already wide awake, washing his whiskers with frantic precision before taking a daring leap from a low branch straight onto James's shoulder.

Together, they set off down the sun-drenched valley trail. The dirt path wound gently between ancient limestone walls and tall golden grasses that swished softly in the morning breeze. Nico darted back and forth with boundless energy—sometimes scrambling along field stones, sometimes riding atop James's pack with his large ears twitching at every passing dragonfly. James paused periodically to check Barnaby's brass pocket compass, watching the polished needle settle steadily toward the south. The distance he had covered no longer felt overwhelming; instead, it felt like a sturdy foundation resting behind his heel.

By mid-day, the trail sloped downward into a calm river basin where an ancient landmark spanned the quiet water: El Puente Viejo, a broad stone bridge built of smooth river cobbles and weathered mortar. The clear water below drifted quietly, reflecting the brilliant blue sky. James climbed onto the wide stone parapet, feeling the deep, sun-baked warmth of the masonry beneath his paws as Nico scrambled up beside him to peer down at tiny river fish swimming below.

Sitting atop the central arch, James carefully unrolled Barnaby's map across the flat stone. In the blank margin far beyond Cloudveil Ridge and Aldea San Gabriel, he took his small piece of charcoal and drew seventy-five fine hash marks along the edge, honoring every step of the road since leaving his treetop home. Nico sniffed the dark charcoal mark with curious delight. Holding his smooth green sea-glass up to his eye, James gazed through the translucent emerald pane at the vast southern valley opening up before them, softly muttering his familiar greeting to the open path ahead: "Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next."
location: El Puente Viejo along the southern valley trail
